text: In 1932, Australia's army went to war... against BIRDS. With machine guns.
Western Australia. Wheat farmers, many of them war veterans, were hit hard by the Depression.
Then around twenty thousand emus showed up... and ate their crops.
So the government sent soldiers. Two Lewis machine guns. Ten thousand rounds.
Day three: over a thousand emus walk up to a dam. Perfect ambush.
The gun kills about a dozen... and JAMS.
They mounted a gun on a truck. The emus outran the truck.
By December, the Major reported 986 kills with 9,860 rounds. EXACTLY ten bullets per bird.
And the emu problem? Still there.
So what actually worked? Not soldiers. Money.
The government kept paying farmers a cash bounty per emu. In six months of 1934, they filed over 57,000 bounty claims.
Turns out the deadliest weapon in that war... wasn't a gun. It was a paycheck.
